evidence.claim: The KD rate as defined mixes causal time ranges, counting as failures some stockouts unrelated to contemporaneous diagnosis; a lag-aware or alternative metric is needed.
evidence.excerpt: The knowing-doing rate as defined mixes two things. KD = Pr(stockout in week t | truly stressed factor named in week t). "Named in week t" is a very local conditioning event; a model that diagnoses in week t and stocks out because of an ordering decision made in weeks t−3..t−1 will count as a KD failure even if its diagnosis-to-action link is instantaneous. The authors acknowledge this ("a stockout in a given week can stem from an ordering decision made weeks earlier") but the metric is still headlined.
